audience: New finance users who need a first tour of where things live in the Odoo Accounting app.
goal: Find your way around the **Accounting** app: open the **Settings**, then visit **Customer Invoices**, **Vendor Bills**, the **Bank and Cash** journals, **Journal Entries**, the **Chart of Accounts**, the **Trial Balance**, and the **Customer** and **Vendor Payments** screens.
before: This guide only **opens** each screen — it does not create or change anything, so you can follow it on a live system.
outcome: You know which top menu each accounting area is under.
You have seen the nine key screens: Settings, Invoices, Bills, Bank and Cash, Journal Entries, Chart of Accounts, Trial Balance, Customer Payments and Vendor Payments.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The numbers you see in the lists (for example how many invoices there are) are test data and will differ from yours.
The red banner at the top of the screenshots ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases.
The top menu in your Odoo may show more or fewer entries than in the screenshots, depending on the apps installed and your access rights.

phases.title: Open Accounting and its Settings
phases.summary: Start the app and look at the company-wide accounting preferences.
phases.checkpoint: You are on the **Settings** screen and have not changed anything.

phases.title: Money owed to you and by you
phases.summary: Customer invoices (Accounts Receivable) and vendor bills (Accounts Payable).
phases.checkpoint: You have seen the customer **Invoices** list and the vendor **Bills** list.

phases.title: Bank, cash and journal entries
phases.summary: Where bank and cash movements are recorded and where every transaction is posted to the ledger.
phases.checkpoint: You have opened **Bank and Cash** and **Journal Entries**.

phases.title: The chart of accounts and the Trial Balance
phases.summary: The list of General Ledger accounts, and the report that proves the books balance.
phases.checkpoint: You have seen the **Chart of Accounts** list and the **Trial Balance** report.

phases.title: Payments
phases.summary: Payments received from customers and payments made to vendors.
phases.checkpoint: You have opened both the **Customer Payments** and **Vendor Payments** lists. The tour is complete.

glossary.meaning: Money your customers owe you. Customer invoices and the payments you receive live here.
Money you owe your suppliers. Vendor bills and the payments you make live here.
A book in which Odoo records one kind of transaction — for example sales, purchases, bank or cash.
A posted accounting transaction made of debit and credit lines. Every invoice, bill and payment ends up as one.
The complete record of all accounts and their movements. The Chart of Accounts is the list of its accounts.
The list of GL accounts. Each has a **code**, a **name** and a **type** (Asset, Liability, Equity, Income, Expense) that decides where it appears on financial reports.
A report listing the debit and credit balance of every GL account for a period, used to check that the books balance before closing.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
1.see: The Accounting app opens with its menu bar across the top (Dashboard, Customers, Vendors, Accounting, Reporting, Configuration …).
1.tip: This is where you manage all finance work: customer invoices, vendor bills, bank transactions, the general ledger and financial reports.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen (the grid of app icons).
Find the **Accounting** icon.
Click it.

2.title: Open the Configuration menu
2.do: In the top menu bar, click **Configuration**.
2.see: A drop-down list of configuration options, including **Settings** and **Chart of Accounts**.
2.where: Accounting app > top menu bar > Configuration
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top of the screen.
Click **Configuration**.

3.title: Open Settings
3.see: The **Settings** screen with **Save** and **Discard** buttons at the top.
3.tip: Settings is where the finance side of Odoo is set up company-wide: fiscal localization, default taxes, currency, invoicing and payment terms. Only change something here if you know what it affects.
actions: With the Configuration menu open, find **Settings** in the list.
Click **Settings**.
Wait for the screen to load — **Save** and **Discard** appear at the top.

4.title: Open the Customers menu
4.do: In the top menu bar, click **Customers**.
4.see: A drop-down with the customer-side screens, including **Invoices** and **Payments**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Customers**.

5.title: Open Customer Invoices
5.see: The list of customer invoices, with **New** and **Upload Invoices** buttons at the top.
5.tip: This is the Accounts Receivable (AR) area: create and manage customer invoices, see what customers owe you, and register incoming payments.
actions: With the Customers menu open, find **Invoices**.
Click **Invoices**.
Wait for the invoice list to load.

6.title: Open the Vendors menu
6.do: In the top menu bar, click **Vendors**.
6.see: A drop-down with the vendor-side screens, including **Bills** and **Payments**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Vendors**.

7.title: Open Vendor Bills
7.see: The list of vendor bills, with **New** and **Upload Bills** buttons at the top.
7.tip: This is the Accounts Payable (AP) area: record vendor bills, see what the company owes suppliers, and process outgoing payments.
actions: With the Vendors menu open, find **Bills**.
Click **Bills**.
Wait for the bill list to load.

8.title: Open the Accounting menu
8.do: In the top menu bar, click **Accounting** (the menu entry, not the app name at the far left).
8.see: A drop-down with the groups Miscellaneous, Journals, Ledgers, Management and Actions.
8.tip: Two things are called "Accounting": the app (left of the menu bar) and this menu entry. You want the menu entry.
actions: Look along the top menu bar for the entry named **Accounting** — not the app name at the far left.
Click it.

9.title: Open Bank and Cash
9.do: In the **Journals** group, click **Bank and Cash**.
9.see: A list of the bank and cash journal items, grouped by journal entry, with the filters **Posted** and **Bank or Cash** already applied.
9.tip: Use this to review deposits and withdrawals. Reconciling bank statements against your accounting records starts from the bank journals.
9.where: Accounting app > Accounting > Journals > Bank and Cash
actions: With the Accounting menu open, find the **Journals** group.
Click **Bank and Cash**.
Wait for the list to load.

10.title: Open the Accounting menu again
10.do: Click **Accounting** in the top menu bar once more.
actions: Look along the top menu bar for **Accounting** again.
Click it.

11.title: Open Journal Entries
11.see: The list of journal entries, with a **New** button and a **Posted** filter.
11.tip: Every financial transaction is posted to the General Ledger here, including manual entries. To make one yourself you would click **New**, add debit and credit lines, then click **Post** — this guide only shows you where the screen is.
11.where: Accounting app > Accounting > Miscellaneous > Journal Entries
actions: With the Accounting menu open, find the **Miscellaneous** group at the top.
Click **Journal Entries**.
Wait for the list to load.

12.title: Open the Configuration menu again
12.do: Click **Configuration** in the top menu bar once more.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Configuration**.

13.title: Open the Chart of Accounts
13.do: In the Configuration menu, click **Chart of Accounts**.
13.see: The list of General Ledger accounts, with **New** and **Import** buttons.
13.tip: Each account has a code, a name and a type (Asset, Liability, Equity, Income, Expense). The type decides how the account appears on financial reports.
13.where: Accounting app > Configuration > Chart of Accounts
actions: With the Configuration menu open, find **Chart of Accounts**.
Click it.
Wait for the list of accounts to load.

14.title: Open the Reporting menu
14.do: In the top menu bar, click **Reporting**.
14.see: A drop-down of financial reports, including **Trial Balance**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Reporting**.

15.title: Open the Trial Balance
15.do: In the Reporting menu, click **Trial Balance**.
15.see: The **Trial Balance** report with **PDF** and **XLSX** buttons and options for the period, comparison, journals and posted entries.
15.tip: It lists the debit and credit balance of every GL account for the period you choose, so you can check the books are balanced before closing.
actions: With the Reporting menu open, find **Trial Balance**.
Click it.
Wait for the report to load.

16.title: Open the Customers menu again
16.do: Click **Customers** in the top menu bar once more.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Customers** again.

17.title: Open Customer Payments
17.see: The **Customer Payments** list, with a **New** button.
17.tip: Register and view payments received from customers, and match them against open invoices (Accounts Receivable).
actions: With the Customers menu open, find **Payments**.
Click it.
Wait for the list of customer payments to load.

18.title: Open the Vendors menu again
18.do: Click **Vendors** in the top menu bar once more.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Vendors** again.

19.title: Open Vendor Payments
19.see: The **Vendor Payments** list, with a **New** button.
19.tip: Register and view payments made to suppliers, and match them against open vendor bills (Accounts Payable). That completes the tour.
actions: With the Vendors menu open, find **Payments**.
Click it.
Wait for the list of vendor payments to load.
